title: The Prize That Vanished on a Shelf
note: Quoted joke in line 3 is a dramatisation. Facts: Hevesy dissolved the Laue and Franck gold medals in aqua regia in Copenhagen in 1940, left the beaker on a lab shelf, and recovered the gold after the war.

lines.text: A scientist dissolved two gold Nobel medals in acid, on purpose
It was nineteen forty, and German soldiers were marching into Denmark, and George had two gold medals he was supposed to guard
So he grabbed a jar and a strong acid, and his friend saw him and laughed, and said, George, you are making soup out of gold
But the acid was so strong that it ate the gold, and the shiny medals turned into orange water
Then he put the jar on a shelf with lots of other jars, and he did not even hide it
Then the soldiers came in, and they went through every drawer, and they looked under every table
You see, it is like the junk drawer in your kitchen, nobody looks in there, because everything in there looks like junk
So the soldiers walked right past the jar, and never touched it
And when the war was over, George turned the orange water back into gold, and the medals were made again
So the man who ruined two Nobel medals on purpose, was the one who saved them
